form_analysis.feedback: Excellent, detailed aftercare for a treatment that actively triggers a healing response. Provides crucial guidance on managing the expected 'purging' phase, distinguishing it from a breakout. Strong emphasis on gentle handling, product restrictions, and sun protection to prevent marks.

form_data.introduction: The following aftercare advice is critical to manage your skin's response, minimise irritation, prevent new breakouts, and reduce the risk of post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation (dark marks) following your intensive acne treatment.

instructions.general_directive: Please follow this aftercare advice diligently. Your skin has undergone a controlled trauma to clear pores and kill bacteria; it now requires gentle, healing-focused care.

sections.title: Immediate Post-Treatment Symptoms and Timeline
sections.content: Your skin will be red, may feel warm, tight, and look shiny/swollen for 24-72 hours. Active acne may appear temporarily more inflamed. Mild peeling or dryness is common 2-5 days post-treatment. A 'purging' phase (see below) is likely.

sections.title: Understanding Purging vs. Breakouts
sections.content: PURGING is a normal, positive response where pre-existing microcomedones (clogged pores under the skin) are accelerated to the surface. It appears as small whiteheads or blackheads, usually in areas where you typically get acne, and clears within 1-2 weeks. A BREAKOUT (reaction) would be new cysts or inflamed pimples in unusual areas, often accompanied by significant irritation.

sections.title: The Golden Rule: Do Not Pick
sections.content: It is imperative that you DO NOT pick, squeeze, or scratch any spots or flaking skin. This can push bacteria deeper, cause scarring, and dramatically increase the risk of dark post-acne marks (PIH).

sections.title: Cleansing and Product Use
items: Cleanse only with a gentle, non-foaming, soap-free cleanser, using lukewarm water and your fingertips only (no cloths or brushes) for the first 3 days.
STOP all other acne medications (benzoyl peroxide, salicylic acid, retinoids, prescription topicals) for 3-5 days or as directed by your therapist.
Use only the soothing, non-comedogenic products recommended by your therapist. A light, oil-free moisturizer is essential to repair the barrier.
Do not use any physical or chemical exfoliants for 7 days.

sections.title: Sun Protection
sections.content: Acne-prone skin healing from inflammation is highly susceptible to pigmentation. You MUST apply a non-comedogenic, oil-free, broad-spectrum SPF 30+ every single morning, even indoors. Sun exposure without protection will darken any red marks left by healing acne.

sections.title: Activity and Environmental Restrictions
items: Avoid sweating (strenuous exercise), saunas, steam, and hot showers for 48-72 hours to prevent further irritation and bacterial spread.
Avoid swimming in chlorinated pools for 48 hours.
Change your pillowcase every other night and keep phone screens clean.

sections.title: Makeup
sections.content: Avoid makeup for 24 hours if possible. If you must wear it, use non-comedogenic, mineral-based products and apply with clean brushes/sponges. Remove it gently.

sections.title: Infection Awareness
sections.content: Contact your therapist immediately if you notice signs of infection: increasing pain, spreading hot redness, yellow pus, or fever. Also contact them if you experience severe, widespread irritation or a blistering rash.

sections.title: General Side Effects and Results Assessment
items: Initial redness and swelling subside in 2-3 days. Purging may occur for 1-2 weeks.
Visible clearing and reduced oiliness are typically seen 1-2 weeks post-treatment. Maximum results are achieved with a consistent course of treatments.
Stay in touch with your therapist to monitor your progress and adjust home care.
